steps.speaker: Thief
steps.content: ...Will everything really be okay?
The chef kept his promise. Early next morning, he confidently hands over the finished product.
To say there are discrepancies from the original would be an understatement. The replica looks like a completely different jar. On closer inspection, it even looks more like a thermos.

steps.speaker: Thief
steps.content: I mean, this is definitely not okay!

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: You can still tell it's a jar... just requires a bit of imagination. Well, it's too late to redo it now. When the merchant returns, we'll just have to make do with what we have.
The chef's product makes it hard for Mira to conceal her worries. She packs this comically shaped replica back into the original bag.
Just as she finishes packing, the disheveled merchant barges into the motel, slamming the wooden door behind him.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Is the innkeeper here? I need to see the innkeeper!!

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Welcome back, sir... Oh my, it's only been a day. How did you end up like this?

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Don't get me started on it. That conman said everyone in his family has a missing tooth, and wanted to knock out my tooth too! He was impossible to reason with. A total lunatic!

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Luckily, I had some cash on me, and that sheriff was easy to deal with. He took the money and let me out. Otherwise, who knows how long I'd be stuck in that lousy detention center!

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Where's my bag with the antique? Oh, it's right here...
At this moment, the still-swaying motel door gets slammed open a second time.

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: Hey! Why are you still here? That drunk "father" of yours realized you escaped from detention and is on his way here! I couldn't stop him!

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: What?!

steps.speaker: Drunkard
steps.content: Ahhhh my son... I'm gonna knock out your tooth to bring you back into the fold! Daddy will be quick about it!

As soon as the sheriff finishes speaking, bloodcurdling shrieks can be heard from outside, getting closer and closer. The merchant's face turns livid. He grabs the bag without checking and rushes out of the motel.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Good. He didn't notice the jar was swapped. You should quickly...
She stops mid-sentence. Mira's reminder is unnecessary, as the thief had already slipped away amidst the chaos.
The shrieks gradually fade away, and the dust stirred by all the running settles down. The chef leisurely walks out from the kitchen, exchanging glances with the sheriff and innkeeper.
After sending off all the guests, the motel returns to its usual quietness, with only the dilapidated wooden door creaking.
Clap! A crisp hand clap breaks the silence.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Alright, that's a wrap. It's just us now. We can stop acting.
Mira rubs her cheeks, stiff from smiling for two days straight. As she looks at the other two, the stagnant atmosphere becomes abuzz with knowing laughter.

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: ...Hahaha, all that acting left me parched. Anything to drink, Mira? With ice, please!
The sheriff drops his imposing demeanor and fans himself with his hat as he lazily leans back on a chair.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: You can have your drink, but let's talk about the door first. How many times have I told you, push the door gently when you enter! If this keeps up, the door will break, and you'll have to pay for it!

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: Yeah yeah... Thanks to that merchant's bribe, I can pay for ten doors.

steps.speaker: Chef
steps.content: Here, Mira, this is your money back to you. Get me a drink too. The usual, please.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Where did you find such a hideous jar? I didn't even know how to keep up with the act!

steps.speaker: Chef
steps.content: That's what jars for pickling meat look like! I've used it for several years now. It's practically an antique!
As they joke and banter, Mira brings out a tray and hands drinks to each of them.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Everything's fine on the other side?

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: I told him to drive that merchant as far away as possible. He really worked hard on his "lunatic dad" act the past two days. When he comes back, we'll treat him to a good meal.

steps.speaker: Chef
steps.content: Absolutely! We must celebrate! It's just a pity about that jar. If we didn't have to smash it, we could've made more money. Maybe it really was an antique.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Oh, who said we smashed it? Look here...
The innkeeper grins slyly. She points to a new cactus plant in an inconspicuous corner of the counter. The pot looks oddly familiar... it's the merchant's jar!

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: That merchant might be dumb, but he has good taste. This jar can genuinely fetch a good price.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: If we add together Wright's bribe, the replica money, and this jar... we made triple the profit from one job!

steps.speaker: Chef
steps.content: Impressive! You have the sharpest eye and wit in town.

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: Alas, the student surpasses the teacher! We really are getting old.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Thanks for the compliment, but you still need to pay what you owe me. Wright, check the time. Korryn should be arriving soon.

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: Alright, alright. Pour me another drink. Once I finish it, I'll go get ready with little Timmy.
Sheriff Wright stretches lazily, puts his hat back on and goes to the door to greet the new guest. Behind him, Mira swiftly rearranges the tableware, her smiling eyes hiding a shifty sparkle.
..."Tuco"?
A girl's gasp echoes from the entrance. The new guest has arrived.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Let's see how much meat we can carve off this plump little lamb.
